audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 2 'why' said 'dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade'. Ambessa's passive stacks no shield, and the line gave no reason why she wins the stage the chart hands her.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund — nothing defensive. Her only shield is Repudiation (W). The real Level 2 edge is Lacerate: dashing out of it strikes a second time, and Infernal Chains is still 20s, so his hold is rarely up.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why and content whys[1] now state Lacerate's second strike and the 20s Infernal Chains gap instead of a shield that does not exist.

audit.why: Spike placement is right: Ambessa at 2-3 (Lacerate dash pattern), 6 (Public Execution, 130s) and Eclipse; Aatrox on Q rank-ups, first item and World Ender at 120s. Content spikes[] and full phases[] agree on all four.

audit.whatIsWrong: The tldr and dosFull[1] told you to 'W-dash' his sweetspots, and Infernal Chains was written as a plain root you 'can't leave'.
audit.why: Ambessa's dashes are Drakehound's Step (P), Lacerate (E) and Public Execution (R); Repudiation is a braced shield that amplifies its slam if it blocked non-minion damage, with no dash on it. Riot's Infernal Chains text: champions 'have to leave the impact area quickly or they will be dragged to the center and take the damage again' — it is an escapable zone, and every one of her three dashes beats the drag.
audit.corrected: tldr and dosFull[1].t now name the real dash and the brace; wants.foe[0] states the leave-the-zone window.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried no numbers — 'matchup-defining', 'your committal tool', 'your ultimate'.
audit.why: The Darkin Blade is 14s at rank 1 and 6s at rank 5; Infernal Chains runs 20s to 12s and is the only thing that can hold Ambessa in a drain trade, so his all-in is gated on W and not on Q; Public Execution is 130s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t now carry rank-1 and rank-5 numbers and name the ability that actually gates his commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warned that Public Execution takes the farthest champion in the line.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Ambessa blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing.' If his jungler is standing behind him you get thrown past Aatrox into both of them, and R costs no energy so you can fire it with nothing left for Q, W or E.
audit.corrected: wants.you[2] now tells you to pick a line clear of his jungler before firing R.

edits.before: Dash-weave his Q — W-dash his sweetspots, combo him. Ambessa wins The Darkin Blade cooldown windows.
edits.after: Dash his Q edges, brace Repudiation on the third swing. Ambessa wins the Infernal Chains cooldown window.

edits.before: Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade. Only take the trade when Aatrox's The Darkin Blade is down.
edits.after: Lacerate strikes a second time if you dash out of it, and Infernal Chains is 20s — step in the moment he spends it.

edits.before: - Aatrox The Darkin Blade: matchup-defining — Sweetspots knock up. Dash them. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - The Darkin Blade: 14s rank 1, 6s rank 5 — sweetspots knock up, dash the edges. - Infernal Chains: 20s to 12s, the only hold on you — his all-in is gated on it, not Q. - Public Execution: 130s, kill windows only.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Lacerate is 13s at rank 1 — a whiffed dash leaves you naked that long.

edits.before: Dumping every dash going IN — Ambessa with no dash left is a duelist who forgot the door.
edits.after: World Ender is 120s and amplifies his healing — never start a long brawl inside it on low HP.

edits.before: Track Aatrox's The Darkin Blade: Sweetspots knock up. Dash them. When it is down — Dash-combo + R him.
edits.after: The Darkin Blade is 14s at rank 1, 6s at rank 5 — dash the edges. Commit when Infernal Chains (20s) is spent.

edits.before: Land all three Q sweetspots into Infernal Chains so you can't leave, turning it into a long drain trade his heal-on-hit wins
edits.after: Tag you with Infernal Chains and hold you in the impact area — leave slowly and the chains drag you back for a second hit

edits.before: Hit Public Execution behind him at 6 so the suppress and armor-pen burst land before World Ender's bonus healing and AD kick in
edits.after: Fire Public Execution down a line clear of his jungler — it takes the FARTHEST champion in it — burst before World Ender heal-amps

edits.before: Q+E gives you a slow-into-trade, but your cooldowns are long and his Deathbringer Stance heals back your chip in any stand-still, so it stays a wash — hit, dash, and refuse the long exchange.
edits.after: At 2 Lacerate's dash strikes a second time and slows, and his Infernal Chains is 20s — hit him the moment he spends it and dash out, so Deathbringer Stance never gets the stand-still it needs to heal.

notes: CHART CONFLICT left alone on purpose: full phases[6].side says Ambessa, content win[6] says Skill, and whys[6] calls the two-item stage a coinflip. Flipping either one breaks the +/-10% length band on a 5- vs 7-character word, so I fixed the prose and left the sides for tools/mirror-fix.js. Ambessa's kit file flags grounding on Repudiation (W) and grounding plus heal on Public Execution (R); Riot's own descriptions of both abilities contain none of that, so I treated them as tooltip-parse misfires ('slams the ground' / 'into the ground') and never told the player W or R denies a dash or heals her. Aatrox's file likewise flags grounding on Infernal Chains while Riot's text says drag and slow only. Suppression versus tenacity, Cleanse or QSS is in neither file, so I made no claim in either direction.
